R7AF-bear-backcountry-0003.name: 670 m NE of Misinchinka River
R7AF-bear-backcountry-0003.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R7AF-bear-backcountry-0003.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Burn from 2021 (fire G61204), 310 m N: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SW facing slope, 12 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland 150 m S: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from District of Tumbler Ridge, about 96 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 55.2589, -122.28481, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 7.1 km SW, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 755 m, about 218 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 220 m SW of the spot at 1,048 m (55.2282, -122.38758). Water: unnamed wetland 120 m SE (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 7-23, Region 7A. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-05, closures 2026-10-16.
